A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WeatherDiffusion, and their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. v2 ends after the references despite referring to supplementary material; v5 includes that material. Added documentation can therefore be identified, without assuming that the underlying experiments or procedures were newly performed.

before.justification: v2 reports original weather-editing comparisons, inverse-rendering measurements, ACDC detection and segmentation results, ablations, and a 61-participant user study.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and supplies additional indoor evaluations, ablation results, user-preference breakdowns, and qualitative analyses in its supplement.

M1.justification: The two-renderer framework, intrinsic map-aware attention, CLIP weather-direction interpolation, heuristic training, and feature distillation are already described in v2 and retained in v5. Supplement C specifies their implementation and training; it does not establish a redesign of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Reported coverage expands beyond driving scenes to indoor training and evaluation using InteriorVerse and Hypersim, which v2 only discusses as existing datasets. Supplement H.3 and Figure 23 also demonstrate non-driving outdoor scenes with people. These extend the represented domains beyond merely adding examples from retained benchmarks.

E2.justification: TurboEdit is newly included as an evaluated weather-removal comparator in supplement F.1 and Figure 9. The original main-table comparator sets remain unchanged, and the indoor evaluation largely reuses the existing inverse-rendering baselines.

E3.justification: The supplementary evaluations add controls crossing IMAA use with additional fine-tuning, plus a control without progressive training. Indoor evaluation assigns four intrinsic maps to InteriorVerse and irradiance to Hypersim. The retained main experiments, metrics, ACDC validation setting, and 61-participant/eight-case study are unchanged; newly specified training settings are implementation disclosures.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's main IMAA and forward-renderer data ablations, v5 supplies stage-specific IMAA controls, heuristic-pretraining analysis, indoor-only training and inverse-renderer WeatherReal ablations, and comparisons of interpolation and feature distillation. It also provides out-of-distribution examples and explicit dense-fog failure cases, substantially expanding the evidence about component necessity and robustness.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The supplementary tables continue point-estimate reporting, and the user-study participant count is unchanged.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. v5 adds indoor results in supplementary Table 4, including 23.58 dB albedo PSNR and 3.11 normal MAE, additional ablation rows, cross-weather consistency values, and user preferences of 77.07% for removal and 86.28% for synthesis. These are newly reported results, not improvements over v2 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The five main-method equations are unchanged. Supplement C.4 and C.6 add explicit mathematical definitions of IMAA supervision and the feature-distillation objective, including its normalized-feature MSE and cosine terms. This is limited formalization of previously described components; no new theorem, proof, or theoretical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about intrinsic-space weather editing, IMAA, the two datasets, and downstream perception benefits. The headline ACDC improvements and claimed advantages over existing approaches are unchanged; the supplement chiefly supplies supporting evidence and details.

C2.justification: The existing temporal-consistency limitation is supplemented by a specific qualification: severe occlusion can cause hallucinated backgrounds and unreliable re-rendered details (supplement I and Figure 25). Sections C.4 and E also explain IMAA collapse without heuristic pretraining and connect distillation to more natural intermediate weather states.

D1.justification: Supplement C–D and G supply substantial previously unavailable implementation information: latent channels, guidance and dropout settings, losses, training stages, learning rates, batch sizes, resolutions, LoRA rank, hardware and runtimes, captioning/filtering procedures, and downstream checkpoints. Dataset release remains promised upon acceptance. The supplement's 35K WeatherSynthetic count conflicts with the retained 38K main-text count, leaving the actual size unresolved.

R1.justification: Supplement A adds historical context on Retinex, prior-based decomposition, and learned inverse rendering. Additional references support implementation choices, datasets, and TurboEdit. The central positioning against pixel-space weather editing and indoor/object-focused rendering methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative, terminology, and section sequence remain essentially verbatim. v5 condenses the author and affiliation block, removes email addresses, and adds separately organized supplementary explanations. The existing argument is not extensively rewritten or reorganized.

P2.justification: The main figure images and table contents are retained but reflowed, with several displays relocated between pages. The supplement adds an architecture diagram, dataset comparison table, expanded ablation and indoor-result tables, and extensive qualitative and failure-case panels. Some material is redisplayed, such as retained ablation rows and Waymo examples, but substantial new visual evidence is supplied.

improvement.justification: v5 resolves substantial documentation and evidential gaps in the supplied v2 by providing implementation details and supporting analyses previously deferred to an absent supplement. Training specifications, component controls, indoor evaluations, and the explicit hallucination failure case make the work substantially easier to reproduce and assess. The unresolved 35K/38K dataset discrepancy detracts from consistency, but does not outweigh these gains; the headline performance results themselves are unchanged.
